newsitem.title: FRANCE: CCF keeps open mind on external growth. [CORRECTED 00:55 GMT 7/3]
newsitem.headline: CCF keeps open mind on external growth. [CORRECTED 00:55 GMT 7/3]

text.p: French bank Credit Commercial de France (CCF) will pursue a strategy of organic growth this year but is not ruling out growth through acquisition, chairman Charles de Croisset said on Thursday.

"1996 is a very good year," he said in a results statement showing a 11.6 (corrects from 7.1) percent rise in 1996 net attributable profit to 1.374 billion francs and a 16 percent hike in the net dividend proposed, to 5.80 francs from 5.00 francs.
"In 1997, CCF will pursue development first of all through internal growth but perhaps by external growth as well," he said in the statement.
"CCF strategy, based on the absolute priority of a solid balance sheet and the profitability of operations, will once again bear fruit, I am sure," he added.
The statement included no other comment regarding 1997.
